comment: Authored routing table for the ReadyVibe Skills marketplace bundle. Every skill named here must be a public skill; every public skill must appear in at least one route (tools/lib/bundle.mjs fails the build otherwise). 'load' is ordered: the first skill is the entry method, later ones are loaded only when their scope applies. Routes are matched top to bottom after an explicit skill name has been ruled out.

routes.request: Whole-site launch readiness: "is this ready to launch / ship / go live?", "make my entire website ready", a pre-launch pass on a vibe-coded site
routes.note: launch-all considers all 40 checks and activates only the specialists that apply. It never runs every skill.

routes.request: Privacy / compliance readiness across the board (GDPR, CCPA, cookies, email, age, deletion)
routes.note: Expect it to refuse the framing "make us compliant": it reports what can be inspected and fixed technically and what needs human or legal review.

routes.request: Everything that decides whether the site can be found: metadata, robots, sitemap, canonicals, social previews, favicon
The site feels unfinished or untrustworthy: dead buttons, placeholders, fake claims, weak 404, no contact path
Combined accessibility and responsive-quality review
Production sweep: forms delivery, unsubscribe, secrets, staging leftovers, headers, performance
SEO: titles, meta descriptions, canonicals, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, indexing
routes.note: seo-readiness is the entry. Load the others only for Search Console setup, structured data, or social previews.

routes.request: Link previews: Open Graph, Twitter/X cards, share images
Structured data / schema.org / JSON-LD / rich results
Search Console / Bing Webmaster setup and verification
Accessibility: keyboard, screen reader, contrast, focus, alt text, labels, zoom, reduced motion
routes.note: Reports observed behavior only; never claims WCAG conformance or a legal accessibility outcome.

routes.request: Mobile and tablet layout: viewport, overflow, navigation, touch targets, forms and tables on small screens
routes.note: Layout fixes change visible UI, so design-system-reconnaissance runs first and the repair is built from the project's own design system.

routes.request: Right-to-left layouts, translations, language switching, hreflang
Performance: oversized assets, blocking scripts, slow loads
Forms and user flows: labels, validation, submission endpoints, loading/success/error states, duplicate submits
routes.note: forms-readiness is the entry. Load failure-resilience for broader loading/empty/error states and email-compliance only when the form feeds email or newsletters.

routes.request: Loading, empty, success and error states; infinite spinners; swallowed errors
Security: exposed secrets, auth, authorization, sessions, private routes, debug endpoints, unsafe redirects
routes.note: web-security is the entry for authentication and authorization audits. Load admin-authorization when admin or operator routes exist, security-headers for HTTPS/headers/CSP, dependency-security for manifests and lockfiles, payments-readiness when money moves. Not a penetration test; never claims a site is secure.

routes.request: HTTPS, redirects, HSTS, response headers, Content-Security-Policy
Vulnerable or suspicious dependencies, lockfiles
Deployment cleanup: localhost/staging URLs, test data, debug routes, source maps, placeholder env values
Broken links, dead CTAs, bad route targets, mailto/tel links
404 / 500 / error pages
Real content: clear purpose and call to action, lorem ipsum, fake testimonials/metrics, unfinished UI
Template leftovers and product identity: starter titles, default favicon, wrong product name, app icons and manifest
An FAQ built from real questions and verified answers
Contact, support and business-identity paths
Reachable legal pages: footer/signup/checkout links to privacy, terms, cookies, refund, accessibility
Write or fix the privacy policy so it matches real behavior
Terms of service / terms of use
Cookies, storage, trackers, consent banner behavior, analytics, third-party scripts
Do the policies, banners and claims match what the product actually does?
What personal data is collected and where it goes; deletion, export, user data rights; data minimization
Marketing email, newsletters, unsubscribe and suppression
Children / age handling, regulated sectors (health, finance, education, legal, crypto, gambling), which markets and laws apply
routes.note: regulated-domain-triggers goes first and may stop ordinary work.

routes.request: Prices, checkout, payments, subscriptions, refunds, consumer-protection basics
AI-powered application readiness: model calls, prompts, keys, disclosure, data sent to AI vendors
User-generated content: posts, comments, uploads, messaging, reporting and moderation hooks
Administrative systems: build or improve an admin, protect admin routes, audit destructive admin actions
routes.note: admin-dashboard builds a full admin tailored to the real app and its design system; admin-authorization protects it; admin-audit-log covers destructive actions.

routes.request: Review a pull request, branch or release for launch and privacy impact
Prove a fix worked; turn evidence into a scoped verdict
Figure out what this site or app actually is and does before changing it
Learn the project's design system before any visible change
